name: ONNX Runtime (transformers GPU inference, BERT and GPT-2)
workload: Average per-inference latency in milliseconds of BERT-base (bert-base-uncased, BertModel, input_ids only) and GPT-2 (GPT2LMHeadModel with past state) on a Tesla V100, batch sizes 1 and 4 (BERT) and 1 to 128 (GPT-2), sequence lengths 8 to 512 (BERT) and 4 to 128 (GPT-2), ORT with graph optimizer script and IO binding.
claimed_speedup: BERT-base, batch 1, fp32: onnxruntime 1.4.0 1.38 ms vs torchscript 1.5.1 7.92 ms at s=8 (5.7x, derived from page data), 3.11 vs 9.56 ms at s=128 (3.1x, derived from page data), 10.74 vs 12.83 ms at s=512 (1.2x, derived from page data); ORT fp16 1.45 ms at s=128 (6.6x vs the torchscript fp32 row, derived from page data). GPT-2, batch 1, fp32: 1.42 vs 5.80 ms at s=4 (4.1x, derived from page data).
compiler_and_flags: Not built from source: prebuilt onnxruntime 1.4.0 (GPU) against PyTorch/TorchScript 1.5.1, so no compiler flags apply. Stated settings: IO binding enabled, ORT transformer optimizer script (graph fusion), fp32 and fp16 rows, run through run_benchmark.sh (benchmark.py) and benchmark_gpt2.py commands printed in the README.
hardware: Tesla V100-PCIE-16GB GPU, CPU Intel Xeon E5-2690 v4
tradeoffs: Needs a model export to ONNX and ORT's transformer optimizer (subgraph pattern matching: the README says layout changes or untested architectures may be only partly optimized). Supported list in the README: BERT, DistilBERT, DistilGPT2, RoBERTa, ALBERT, GPT-2 (PyTorch) and BERT (TensorFlow). Many execution providers and bindings (C, C++, Python, C#, Java, JS), larger binary than a plain PyTorch install.
caveats: Numbers are from ORT 1.4.0 and PyTorch 1.5.1 (2020 era); newer PyTorch (torch.compile, SDPA kernels) and newer ORT are not in the table, so the gap today is unknown. The baseline is TorchScript only (no TensorRT, no PyTorch eager row in the table). The advantage shrinks to 1.2x at s=512 batch 1. The fp16 rows are ORT fp16 against the torchscript fp32 row (no torchscript fp16 row). The README table is for bert-base-uncased while the current run_benchmark.sh default model list is bert-base-cased, roberta-base and distilbert-base-uncased with sequence lengths up to 1024, so the exact script version behind the table is not pinned. First-party (Microsoft) measurement; compiler is not applicable to prebuilt wheels, so A rests on public scripts plus stated hardware and versions. The README states the results were obtained with the optimizer and IO binding enabled.
found_via: seed-record pass: started from https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime (awesome-cpp Machine Learning list), then onnxruntime/python/tools/transformers/README.md and run_benchmark.sh

name: PlayRho
workload: Google Benchmark microbenchmarks in the project's Benchmark/BenchmarkMain.cpp, built with BENCHMARK_BOX2D defined: one world step with N static bodies, N non-colliding falling disks, a 400-count broad-phase pair stress test and a tile-dropping scene, PlayRho vs Box2D.
claimed_speedup: Latest wiki run (commit ef285b19a, 2021-05-25), PlayRho vs Box2D time per iteration: WorldStepWithStatsStatic/10000 67,606 ns vs 329,934 ns (4.9x, derived from page data); DropDisks/1000 384,976 ns vs 874,668 ns (2.3x, derived from page data); DropDisks/10000 3,837,606 ns vs 6,266,863 ns (1.6x, derived from page data); AddPairStressTest400/18 48,679,814 ns vs 106,326,260 ns (2.2x, derived from page data); TilesRestOneGround/36 1,195,594,385 ns vs 1,445,217,889 ns (1.2x, derived from page data). PlayRho is slower on TilesRestComboGround/36 (1,418,653,021 ns vs 1,329,953,352 ns) and /12 (22,889,731 ns vs 18,891,740 ns). Author comment on the page: 'PlayRho often faster than Box2D and in tests I'd expect PlayRho to be faster in'.
hardware: '2.6 GHz Intel Core i7' (wiki page title), 8 X 2600 MHz CPUs per Google Benchmark header; exact CPU model not stated
tradeoffs: 2-D only; began as a port of Box2D 2.3.2 and is now a derivative with a different API (value semantics, no pointers, strongly typed units optional, configurable Real type including double and fixed point). Master branch interface is not stable (use tagged releases or release branches). Needs a C++17 compiler.
caveats: First-party numbers from a wiki page that the project README only points to as 'benchmark data'; compiler, flags and build type are not stated (output ends with 'Program ended with exit code: 0', Xcode-style, but nothing confirms it). The Box2D rows exist only if BENCHMARK_BOX2D is defined by editing BenchmarkMain.cpp (the define is commented out) and Box2D is linked by hand; the Box2D version is stated as 2.4.1 for the earlier commit-00991d1ec run, not for the ef285b19a run. The scenes are small microbenchmarks: WorldStepWithStatsStatic steps static bodies only, and in DropDisks the disks are spaced 2 m apart with radius 0.5 so no contacts form (measures integration and broad phase, not contact solving). PlayRho's step is fully configurable per call while Box2D uses Step(1/60, 8, 3). The same page's earlier run (commit 00991d1ec) showed PlayRho about 100x faster on AddPairStressTest400/18 (1,120,420 ns vs 104,630,145 ns) and the author called that surprising and not trustworthy; the later run gives 2.2x. Wins are mixed: PlayRho loses the TilesRestComboGround rows. The listed guess of ODE or Bullet as baseline was wrong; the only comparison is against Box2D, its ancestor.
